aisec: AI-assisted offensive tooling is hitting core security infrastructure: Check Point management servers and Palo Alto firewalls were compromised, and an Anthropic-scanner-found Drupal flaw is now exploited.
Agentic attack frameworks are spreading: Microsoft says ARTEX is used by Chinese and North Korean groups, while Cisco Talos and Swiss and Italian agencies warn of autonomous AI-driven attacks.
Research covers AI system weaknesses: agent auditing, Rowhammer backdoors in DNN models, model-as-a-service assurance, LLM watermarking, telecom LLM risks and deception that raises attacker costs.
ai: Agentic AI is driving access disputes and attacks: Amazon and Meta reportedly discuss ending the Muse shopping agent block, while AI-assisted hacking incidents and swarm tradecraft draw scrutiny.
AI infrastructure and governance face pressure: neoclouds struggle with data center delays and costlier debt, and Nvidia faces questions over Megaspeed chip diversion and leadership liability.
AI is spreading into products and public systems: recording earbuds raise privacy concerns, AI-driven demand strains open records offices, and vibe coding enables synthesizer firmware modding.
cyber: Critical flaws are under active exploitation: Drupal RCE (Fail2Install), GeoServer chains, and a CVSS 10.0 Hex.pm bug that compromised six package registry servers, so patch quickly.

Supply-chain and identity attacks continue: backdoored WordPress plugins, malicious NuGet packages aimed at .NET developers, appliance third-party component flaws, and Com-affiliated vishing for cloud account takeover.

Government and enterprise incidents persist: FinCEN took systems offline after an intrusion, a CIA analysis system was reportedly breached, and Microsoft's November updates caused authentication problems.
